checks: At a feasible point all of the first k inequalities are strictly below 1/k, so continuity gives an open neighborhood hit by the dense sequence. Conversely, for a fixed parameter with all approximants, compactness provides a convergent subsequence with indices tending to infinity. Each fixed constraint then holds at the limit.

The feasible parameter set is the intersection over k of countable unions of Borel inequalities evaluated at fixed dense points. Least successful indices and their point evaluations are Borel on this set, including if the dense sequence repeats points.

A finite cover of diameter at most 2 to the power minus m exists by compactness, using sufficiently small closed balls. At each step the prior intersection contains infinitely many approximant indices, so some member of the next finite cover retains infinitely many indices. Membership in the prior selected finite intersection is Borel by induction on its finite-valued choices. The infinitely-often predicate is a countable intersection of countable unions.

The retained intersections are nonempty, compact and nested. Diameter tends to zero, so the intersection is a singleton. Selecting the least retained k at least m is Borel and converges to this singleton, which is feasible because the selected indices tend to infinity. The Borel complement accepts a fixed value since X is nonempty.
